- **A public key needs its allowlist.** A new game has no traffic to suggest event names from, and a key with an empty allowlist refuses every event while still holding a place. Send `policy.allowed_events` with at least one of the names the game sends, read from its code, or the call answers `400 allowed_events_required`. `label`, `expiresAt` and the rest of the [policy](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/public-builds/#public-policy) are optional. At two live public keys the call answers `409 public_key_limit`; `org_revoke_public_key` frees a place by the key's prefix.
 
- **A live key replaces the old one.** For a game whose key has already been used, every build using the old key stops reporting at once. In the four internal environments, `development`, `staging`, `alpha` and `beta`, the call needs `"rotate": true` and answers `409 rotate_required` without it. There, a game whose key has never been used needs no flag. In every other environment a key that has never been used also needs `"rotate": true`: a build already shipped with it and not yet reporting, such as one waiting in store review, stops reporting when the key is replaced, and nothing on the server can see that build, so confirm with the studio first. A key counts as used once any build has authenticated with it: an event, a remote config read, a player account call, a session, or a request refused after the key was recognised.
 
- **A build the public plays stays in the dashboard.** In `production`, `early-access`, `demo` and any environment you named yourself, the live key of a game whose key has been used is rotated in Settings only, and so is revoking one of its public keys. Both answer `409 key_dashboard_only`, with or without `rotate`. An agent cannot move such a game to an internal environment either, or change the environment of a used `production` game at all (`409 environment_locked`).
 
- **The claim is the credential.** `POST /api/v1/data/org/key-claims/redeem` takes no token, only the code in the `X-Ravensight-Claim` header, never in a URL. It checks again that the token that issued the claim is live and still has both permissions, and that its holder still has the role. An unknown, used or expired code answers `404 claim_not_found`, the same answer in every case. A valid code can still answer `409` with `rotate_required`, `key_dashboard_only`, `public_key_limit`, `invalid_expires_at` or `steam_connection_missing` when things changed after the claim was issued, and the claim is kept for another try. If creating the key fails part way the answer is `500 claim_spent`: issue a new claim. It allows 5 tries per claim from one address and 20 per address in 10 minutes, then answers `429 rate_limited`.
 
- **What it costs.** Each of the three tools is one programmatic call, 100,000 weighted events on the shared event meter, like every other organization operation. Redeeming the claim has no charge of its own.
 
- **Retries.** Repeating `org_issue_key` with the same operation ID answers the same claim and cannot create a second key. A lost redemption answer is not retried: issue a new claim. A lost public key still holds one of the two places until you revoke it.
 
- **What the file is not.** It keeps the key out of the conversation by default. It is not a security boundary: an agent that can read the disk can read the file. An engine that does not read environment variables, such as a Godot script with an exported `ingest_key`, still needs the key placed in the project or the build step, which is expected for a key that ships inside a build.
 
- **The trail.** Your audit log records the issue with the key's kind, and the redemption and a revoke with the kind and the prefix. A redeemed live key also appears as a key rotation, and a public key as created or revoked, the same entries the dashboard writes. The key, the claim code and the policy are never written to it.

documents.section_title: Desktop pets with their own studio chat
documents.title: Desktop pets with their own studio chat
documents.content:
19. Raven

 

## Desktop pets with their own studio chat

 

Huginn and Muninn stay quietly on your desktop. Click a raven to open Raven’s chat and ask the same Huginn analyst you use in the dashboard, drawing on your studio’s data and memory. Questions use your studio’s shared AI allowance and prepaid balance. Get the installers from the [Raven download page](https://www.ravensight.io/raven/).

 

Raven and [Skill Activity](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/skill-activity-desktop/) are separate apps with independent settings, credentials and lifecycles. Raven keeps its pets and chat; Skill Activity follows local agent work. Install either or both.

documents.section_title: Desktop pets with their own studio chat
documents.title: Install the beta
documents.content:
### Install the beta

 

1. [Download the installer for your platform](https://www.ravensight.io/raven/).
 
1. On Apple Silicon macOS, open the ZIP and drag Ravensight to Applications, then open the app.
 
1. On Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit x64, run the setup EXE.
 
1. Check the file against the published [SHA-256 checksums](https://www.ravensight.io/downloads/raven/0.3.0-rc.2/SHA256SUMS.txt) before you open it.

 

Windows 0.2.3 is not publisher signed, so operating-system or organization policy may block it. Keep your security protections enabled. Broader machine compatibility checks remain in progress for the Mac release candidate.

documents.section_title: Desktop pets with their own studio chat
documents.title: Connect
documents.content:
### Connect

 

The desktop app offers three ways to reach your studio. It keeps whichever credential you use in your operating system's credential store.

 

| Method | Credential | Who answers | What it uses |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sign in | Device approval in the dashboard | The hosted analyst | Your studio's AI allowance, then prepaid balance |
| Analyst API key | `gt_raven_...` | The hosted analyst | Your studio's AI allowance, then prepaid balance |
| Your own model key | Provider API key and `gt_mcp_...` | A model you call from your own machine | Your provider's charges, plus metered MCP reads |

 

1. **Sign in:** choose Connect Ravensight. Your browser opens a device approval page. Sign in, check that the code matches the one the app shows, choose which games the desktop app may ask about, and approve. An unapproved code expires after ten minutes.
 
1. **Analyst API key:** create a key under [Settings > Desktop](https://app.ravensight.io/settings/desktop) and paste the `gt_raven_` key into the app. The dashboard shows the key once. It uses the same hosted analyst and billing as signing in.
 
1. **Your own model key:** choose **Bring your own AI** and enter an Anthropic API key, a model ID your key can use, and a Ravensight MCP key from **Settings > MCP access** (see [Analytics MCP](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/mcp/)). Both keys stay on your device. Your question, and the studio data the desktop app reads to answer it, go from your machine to Anthropic under your own account. The read-only loop is bounded to six model calls and twelve MCP calls per question.

 

The own-key option is the one place Ravensight works with a key you hold, and it exists only in this desktop client. Ravensight never receives or stores your provider key; the hosted analyst and every other feature run on Ravensight's own platform key, as described in [Usage, billing and limits](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/limits/).

documents.section_title: Desktop pets with their own studio chat
documents.title: Usage and access
documents.content:
### Usage and access

 

- Downloading the client is free and does not include free or unmetered AI.
 
- A hosted question, by sign-in or analyst API key, is billed like a dashboard question: one shared AI unit, drawn from the studio's included monthly allowance first and then its prepaid balance, on the studio owner's account.
 
- With your own model key, your provider bills you for the model calls, and each Ravensight MCP read is weighted as 100,000 events on the studio's shared event meter. MCP needs an account that has funded a prepaid balance at least once, and your MCP token's own budget still applies.
 
- Asking needs a role that can ask the analyst, member or above. Desktop app credentials can ask questions and read your own conversation history; they cannot edit studio memory or delete conversations.
 
- Desktop app tokens and keys can be revoked and expire after 90 days. Every call rechecks your membership and role, so a removed member or revoked credential stops working at once.
 
- A game allowlist restricts which games the desktop app can ask about. Shared studio memory may still inform an answer, so the allowlist is not a data boundary inside one studio.

documents.section_title: Desktop pets with their own studio chat
documents.title: Controls and activity
documents.content:
### Controls and activity

 

The ravens rest, blink independently and occasionally glance around. Click either bird, or Expand, to open or close chat; the birds work from the keyboard too. Drag either bird to reposition the widget. The toolbar opens chat, activity and settings. Activity shows the real progress of a request, its answer and any error. Settings shows one or both ravens, pauses animation and checks for updates by hand. The desktop app respects your system's reduced motion setting. Voice and autonomous desktop control are not included.

documents.section_title: Desktop pets with their own studio chat
documents.title: Recover an interrupted question
documents.content:
### Recover an interrupted question

 

The desktop app saves a hosted question's request ID before sending it. If the app closes mid-answer, use **Recover same request** after a restart. Recovery replays the answer the server already produced and cannot start another paid operation; a request the server has not finished is refused rather than run twice. Saved answers expire after seven days and are removed when their conversation or game is deleted. Once one is gone, recovery is unavailable and does not charge you again.

 

Dismiss recovery only when you choose to move on: a new question is a separate billed operation. Questions asked with your own model key are never retried automatically.

documents.section_title: Desktop pets with their own studio chat
documents.title: Updates and revocation
documents.content:
### Updates and revocation

 

**Settings, Check for updates** reads the official release manifest. Install updates from the [download page](https://www.ravensight.io/raven/); this beta never installs updates silently. Disconnect removes the local connection. Revoke a lost or unused device or key on the [Desktop tab in Settings](https://app.ravensight.io/settings/desktop), and never share your API keys.

documents.section_title: Desktop pets with their own studio chat
documents.title: Troubleshooting
documents.content:
### Troubleshooting

 

A 401 usually means you need to reconnect or create a new key. Permission or balance errors mean checking your studio role and your usage settings. Keep the API and dashboard addresses at their defaults unless you are deliberately connecting to your own development environment.

documents.section_title: Follow local skills in a separate Mac app
documents.title: Follow local skills in a separate Mac app
documents.content:
Skill Activity

 

## Follow local skills in a separate Mac app

 

Ravensight Skill Activity shows skill invocations, sessions and reported results for projects you choose. It is a standalone application, separate from [Raven and its pets](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/raven-desktop/). Local monitoring needs no login.

documents.section_title: Follow local skills in a separate Mac app
documents.title: Install and choose a project
documents.content:
### Install and choose a project

 

1. [Download Skill Activity for Apple Silicon Mac](https://www.ravensight.io/skill-activity/) and compare it with the published checksum.
 
1. Open the ZIP, drag **Ravensight Skill Activity** to Applications and open it. This does not replace the Ravensight app used by Raven.
 
1. Choose your project folder. Review the hook setup before installing it, then run your coding agent in that project.
 
1. Use the timeline and filters to inspect sessions, skills and evidence types. Pause collection from the project controls when you want to stop monitoring.

 

There is no Windows Skill Activity release yet. Raven’s Windows installer is a different product and does not provide Skill Activity.

documents.section_title: Follow local skills in a separate Mac app
documents.title: Hide, reopen or quit
documents.content:
### Hide, reopen or quit

 

Closing the Skill Activity window hides it while the app stays available in the macOS menu bar. Choose **Open Skill Activity** there to return, or **Quit Skill Activity** to exit it. Quitting Raven does not quit Skill Activity, and quitting Skill Activity does not quit Raven.

documents.section_title: Follow local skills in a separate Mac app
documents.title: Read the evidence correctly
documents.content:
### Read the evidence correctly

 

An observed invocation records that a skill ran. A producer-reported result records what the agent reported, such as checks passed. Reported outcomes are labelled and are not independent verification. Loading a skill does not prove its work is complete.

 

The activity feed excludes prompts, source code and tool output. The Apache-2.0 [telemetry core, Claude adapter and registry](https://github.com/Reality-Software-Entertainment/ravensight-skill-telemetry) are open source; the desktop app and cloud integration are separate.

documents.section_title: Follow local skills in a separate Mac app
documents.title: Optional cloud history and its cost
documents.content:
### Optional cloud history and its cost

 

Sign in using your existing Ravensight account, approve the connection and select a game for sharing. This connection belongs to Skill Activity; it does not reuse Raven’s connection. Cloud sharing requires explicit project consent and can be switched off while local monitoring continues.

 

- Each newly accepted normalized record uses **1,000 weighted events** on your studio’s existing event meter, drawing from the included allowance first.
 
- Prepaid spending starts off and needs separate explicit consent. Without that consent, sharing stops when the included allowance is unavailable.
 
- Cloud history lasts seven days, with a bounded 1,000 admissions per game. It never enters player analytics.
 
- Deleting cloud history does not erase local records. Retrying the same deleted record cannot restore it or charge again during its original retention window.

 

You can disconnect or revoke the app’s connection to stop cloud access. Your local activity remains available. Downloading Skill Activity or reading local history does not use AI units.

documents.section_title: Read game data over REST
documents.title: Read game data over REST
documents.content:
Programmatic access

 

## Read game data over REST

 

Use your existing scoped MCP token with the Ravensight API. Each game-data request has the same price as an MCP read: 100,000 weighted events on the shared event meter. A studio must have funded a prepaid balance. `GET /api/v1/data/games` is free. This surface requires usage billing V2 to be enabled.

 

Send the token only in the Authorization header. Tokens in query strings are rejected. Existing studio membership, role, project and tool restrictions still apply. Reuse an operation ID only to retry the exact same request; completed retries do not charge again.

 

```
curl https://api.ravensight.io/api/v1/data/games/GAME_ID/overview \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RAVENSIGHT_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Ravensight-Operation-Id: overview-request-001"
```

 

Under `/api/v1/data/games/:gameId/`, read `metrics`, `overview`, `retention`, `funnel`, `breakdown`, `monetization`, `economy`, `health`, `progression`, `distribution` and `events`. Pass `from` and `to` in Unix seconds, at most 31 days apart. Funnel steps and retention days accept comma-separated values. Property filters accept a JSON object.

 

Event pages contain up to 1,000 rows in the shared export schema. Continue with `after=nextAfter&skip=nextSkip` until `nextAfter` is null. The cursor timestamp is in milliseconds. Offsets are bounded to 1,000; use bucket export for bulk archival or a timestamp containing more rows than this bounded reader can page. Synthetic events are excluded by default; `include_synthetic=include` or `only` changes that scope.

 

Responses carry `meta` plus `X-Ravensight-Operation-Id`, `X-Ravensight-Event-Units` and `X-Ravensight-Rate-Version`. A query is bounded to 128,000 response bytes. The rate limit is 300 requests per minute per token. Unknown and inaccessible games both return 404. [Download the OpenAPI 3.1 specification](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/openapi/data-v1.json).

documents.section_title: Warehouse SQL over REST
documents.title: Warehouse SQL over REST
documents.content:
## Warehouse SQL over REST

 

Send `POST /api/v1/data/games/{gameId}/sql` to the existing Ravensight API with your studio-bound programmatic token in the Authorization header. The JSON body contains `sql` and optional `include_synthetic` (exclude, include or only). The same SELECT-only guard as [run_sql](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/run-sql/) rewrites every events-table reference to your game. It cannot read another game, other tables, credentials or external URLs. Standard MCP run_sql limits are unchanged.

 

The warehouse profile allows up to 10,000 result rows, 30 seconds, 1 GB read, one billion scanned rows and a 4 MB response. Each token may start 200 warehouse queries per UTC day. An estimate above one billion rows is refused before reservation. Role, project, tool allowlist, prepaid funding and token-cap checks still apply.

 

**Price:** `(2 + ceil(rows read / 500000)) × 100000` weighted events. Before execution, Ravensight estimates the guarded scan and reserves that amount. If actual scanning uses fewer calls, the difference is refunded once; a larger actual scan never increases the reservation. When actual row statistics are unavailable, the reservation is retained and the response says so. Refused execution is refunded. Use the same `X-Ravensight-Operation-Id` on identical retries to reuse the stored result and charge.

 

| Rows read | Calls | Weighted events | After included events |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 2 | 200,000 | $0.10 |
| 500,000 | 3 | 300,000 | $0.15 |
| 1,200,000 | 5 | 500,000 | $0.25 |

 

```
{ "sql": "SELECT event_name, count() AS events FROM events GROUP BY event_name ORDER BY events DESC LIMIT 20", "include_synthetic": "exclude" }
```

 

The response includes scanned rows, the estimate, reserved and charged calls, and normal operation metadata. Audit rows record IDs and scan counts, excluding SQL text. [OpenAPI specification](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/openapi/data-v1.json).

documents.section_title: Connect a BI tool
documents.title: Connect a BI tool
documents.content:
Programmatic access

 

## Connect a BI tool

 

There are two ways to put Ravensight numbers in a reporting tool. Both work today, and the guides below give the steps for Looker Studio, Tableau, Power BI and Metabase.

 

- **Your own warehouse, fed by bucket export.** [Bucket export](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/bucket-export/) writes every event to your own S3 bucket as Parquet or gzip JSON lines, in folders named `game_id=`, `dt=` and `hour=`. You load or attach those files in a database or warehouse you run, then point the BI tool at it with that tool's own connector. This is the route for event-level reporting and large volumes. Each exported event counts as five events on your shared event meter.
 
- **The REST data API.** [Read game data over REST](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/data-api/) answers the same metrics the dashboard shows (`metrics`, `retention`, `funnel`, `monetization` and more) as JSON, for a window of at most 31 days per request. This is the route for small summary tables. Every request that reads a game costs one programmatic call, 100,000 events on the shared event meter, about $0.05 once the included allowance is spent, so a report that refreshes often adds up: each refresh of each table is one request.

 

**The token.** The REST API takes a studio-bound MCP token from **Settings > MCP access**, sent only in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer gt_mcp_...`. A token in the URL is refused. For a reporting tool, mint a token for this purpose only, limit it to the tools the report reads and to the projects it needs, and set a monthly spending cap on it. The studio must have funded a prepaid balance once. Anyone who can open the report's data source settings can see the token, so treat the report file like the token.

 

Money in the REST answers is whole minor units of one currency (`revenue: 1999` with `minorUnitDigits: 2` is 19.99). Divide by 10 to the power of `minorUnitDigits` to display it, and never add two currencies together.

documents.section_title: Looker Studio
documents.title: Looker Studio
documents.content:
Connect a BI tool

 

## Looker Studio

documents.section_title: Looker Studio
documents.title: From your own warehouse
documents.content:
### From your own warehouse

 

1. Set up [bucket export](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/bucket-export/) to your S3 bucket, in Parquet if your warehouse reads it.
 
1. Load the exported files into a database Looker Studio has a connector for, such as PostgreSQL, MySQL or a Google Cloud warehouse, on a schedule that suits you. The hourly `_ravensight_manifest.json` lists each new file and its row count.
 
1. In Looker Studio, choose **Create**, then **Data source**, and pick the connector for that database.
 
1. Enter the database's connection details and choose the table that holds the events.
 
1. Build the report on its columns: `event`, `tsIso`, `platform`, `gameVersion` and the rest of the [row schema](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/bucket-export/).

documents.section_title: Looker Studio
documents.title: From the REST data API, through a Google Sheet

documents.section_title: Tableau
documents.title: Tableau
documents.content:
Connect a BI tool

 

## Tableau

documents.section_title: Tableau
documents.title: From your own warehouse
documents.content:
### From your own warehouse

 

1. Set up [bucket export](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/bucket-export/) and load or attach the files in a database or warehouse Tableau has a connector for.
 
1. In Tableau, under **Connect**, choose **To a Server** and pick that database's connector.
 
1. Sign in with the database's own credentials and drag the events table onto the canvas.
 
1. Use `tsIso` as the date field and `event`, `platform` and `gameVersion` as dimensions.

documents.section_title: Tableau
documents.title: From the REST data API, through a saved file
documents.content:
### From the REST data API, through a saved file

 

Tableau reads JSON files, so a scheduled command saves the answer and Tableau connects to the file.

 

1. Put your token in an environment variable named `RAVENSIGHT_TOKEN` on the machine that runs the command.
 
1. Run the command below, replacing `GAME_ID`, and schedule it with your system's scheduler.
 
1. In Tableau, under **Connect**, choose **To a File**, **JSON file**, and open `retention.json`.
 
1. Select the `cohorts` schema level to get one row per first-seen cohort with its `d1` and `d7`.
 
1. Refresh the extract after each scheduled run.

 

```
curl -sf https://api.ravensight.io/api/v1/data/games/GAME_ID/retention \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RAVENSIGHT_TOKEN" -o retention.json
```

documents.section_title: Power BI
documents.title: Power BI
documents.content:
Connect a BI tool

 

## Power BI

documents.section_title: Power BI
documents.title: From your own warehouse
documents.content:
### From your own warehouse

 

1. Set up [bucket export](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/bucket-export/) and load or attach the files in a database or warehouse Power BI has a connector for.
 
1. In Power BI Desktop, choose **Get data** and pick that database's connector.
 
1. Enter the server and database, sign in with the database's own credentials, and select the events table.
 
1. Choose **Load**, or **Transform data** to shape it first.

documents.section_title: Power BI
documents.title: From the REST data API
documents.content:
### From the REST data API

 

The Web connector in Power BI Desktop can send the `Authorization` header itself.

 

1. Choose **Get data**, **Web**, then **Advanced**.
 
1. In the URL parts, enter `https://api.ravensight.io/api/v1/data/games/GAME_ID/metrics` with your game id.
 
1. Under the HTTP request header parameters, add `Authorization` with the value `Bearer gt_mcp_...`.
 
1. When asked how to connect, choose **Anonymous**: the header carries the token.
 
1. In Power Query, expand the record into columns and choose **Close & Apply**. Each refresh is one request per query.

documents.section_title: Metabase
documents.title: Metabase
documents.content:
Connect a BI tool

 

## Metabase

 

Metabase reads databases, not web APIs, so both routes end in a database.

documents.section_title: Metabase
documents.title: From your own warehouse
documents.content:
### From your own warehouse

 

1. Set up [bucket export](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/bucket-export/) and load or attach the files in a database Metabase supports, such as PostgreSQL or MySQL.
 
1. In Metabase, open **Admin settings**, **Databases**, and choose **Add database**.
 
1. Pick the database type, enter its connection details and save. Metabase scans the tables.
 
1. Start a new question on the events table, or write SQL against it in the native query editor.

documents.section_title: Metabase
documents.title: From the REST data API
documents.content:
### From the REST data API

 

1. Create a table in a database Metabase already reads, for example `ravensight_metrics(read_at, players, sessions, new_players, returning_players)`.
 
1. Write a scheduled job that calls `GET /api/v1/data/games/GAME_ID/metrics` with the `Authorization: Bearer` header and inserts one row per run.
 
1. Add that database in Metabase as above, if it is not there yet, and build questions on the table.

documents.section_title: Your events, delivered to your own bucket
documents.title: Your events, delivered to your own bucket
documents.content:
27. Bucket export

 

## Your events, delivered to your own bucket

 

Bucket export supports gzip JSON Lines or Parquet with quarter-hour delivery once your S3 destination is configured and enabled. Add the bucket policy shown in **Settings > Exports** and test the connection. Only the studio owner can add, change, pause or disable an export. Google Cloud Storage is not currently available.

documents.section_title: Your events, delivered to your own bucket
documents.title: Future Google Cloud Storage setup
documents.content:
### Future Google Cloud Storage setup

 

This provider cannot currently be enabled. When available, grant the studio-specific service account shown in the dialog a custom bucket role with `storage.objects.create` and `storage.objects.delete`, restricted to your export prefix. Replacement permission is needed for delivery retries and hourly manifest updates. No read or list permission is required. The service account must first be provisioned by the platform operator; no customer credential file is uploaded.

documents.section_title: Your events, delivered to your own bucket
documents.title: What it costs
documents.content:
### What it costs

 

Configuration, connection tests and delivery require a positive prepaid balance. Your included event allowance still applies. Each exported event counts as five events on your shared event meter, so 100,000 exported events are 500,000 events, $0.25 once the included allowance is spent. Nothing is charged for an hour with no events, a refused write is refunded, and a retry is never charged twice. Each export has a monthly cap of 20,000,000 exported events by default (set it to 0 for no cap); an export writes up to it and then pauses until the first of next month or until you raise it. If your balance cannot cover the next file, the export pauses with the reason shown, we email the owner once, and it picks up exactly where it stopped once funded. Late-arriving events are picked up by the regular quarter-hour delivery using the time Ravensight received them. No debt is carried.

documents.section_title: Your events, delivered to your own bucket
documents.title: Granting S3 access

documents.section_title: Your events, delivered to your own bucket
documents.title: Layout
documents.content:
### Layout

 

One file per page of up to 10,000 events, never crossing a UTC ingestion hour, plus a manifest per hour listing its files and row counts:

 

```
<prefix>/game_id=<gameId>/dt=2026-10-15/hour=09/1760518800000-1760522400000.jsonl.gz
<prefix>/game_id=<gameId>/dt=2026-10-15/hour=09/_ravensight_manifest.json

{ "schema": 1, "gameId": "<gameId>",
  "files": [ { "file": "1760518800000-1760522400000.jsonl.gz", "rows": 8421, "bytes": 702113 } ] }
```

 

The folders are named key=value partitions, so a query engine reading the bucket sees `game_id`, `dt` and `hour` as columns. The two numbers in a file name are the page's start and end in epoch milliseconds.

 

Parquet files use the same partition layout with `.parquet` instead of `.jsonl.gz`, the same manifest and the same price. Their fixed schema has scalar columns, `ts` as TIMESTAMP_MILLIS, nullable typed `rs_*` columns, and `props`, `data` and `rs` as JSON text. Unknown properties and experiment tags remain in the raw JSON rather than adding columns. Invalid typed values remain in raw JSON and do not populate trusted typed columns.

documents.section_title: Your events, delivered to your own bucket
documents.title: Row schema
documents.content:
### Row schema

 

Each JSON line is one event in the same shape as the [raw event export](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/limits/): `schema` (currently 1), `gameId`, `deviceId`, `sessionId`, `event`, `ts` (epoch milliseconds), `tsIso`, `level`, `platform`, `gameVersion`, `country`, `deviceModel`, `osVersion`, `gpu`, `synthetic`, `props`, `data` (the stored payload text), `rs` (the typed event contract), and `campaign`, `adset` and `creative` (where the device was acquired, null when it was not attributed). Keys are only ever added, so read the ones you know and ignore the rest. Playtest sessions are left out unless you include them.

documents.section_title: Your events, delivered to your own bucket
documents.title: Backfill and timing
documents.content:
### Backfill and timing

 

Choose "include the last 90 days" when you add an export to start from the oldest events Ravensight still keeps; the dialog estimates what that costs first. After that, each quarter hour writes what arrived up to a minute ago.

documents.section_title: Your events, delivered to your own bucket
documents.title: Duplicates
documents.content:
### Duplicates

 

A write that succeeded but reported a failure is retried to the same file name, and in rare cases a row can appear in two files. Dedupe on `sessionId`, `ts`, `event` and `data`. Disabling an export keeps every file it wrote.

 

Owners can also read delivery history through the `list_export_deliveries` MCP tool. It uses the same game and owner permissions as the dashboard, returns up to 50 deliveries per page, and accepts `before` from the returned `nextCursor`. It cannot create, change or start an export. Standard MCP usage charges apply.

documents.section_title: Extended raw-event retention
documents.title: Extended raw-event retention
documents.content:
## Extended raw-event retention

 

Studio owners can choose 90, 180 or 400 days in each game's Settings. The default is 90 days. A longer window preserves raw events that remain in storage; it cannot recover expired data. Lifetime aggregate history is separate, and existing programmatic query limits still apply.

 

**Reading retained data:** Monetization, Economy, Health, Builds, Progression, Retention and Explore offer 180- and 400-day dashboard ranges when the game's storage setting supports them. Retention uses weekly cohorts for ranges longer than 90 days so the full window fits; Explore keeps its 14-day limit for hourly grouping. Overview still uses aggregate history for ranges beyond 90 days; extending storage does not turn those views into raw-event queries or rebuild expired history. Structured MCP and REST analytics requests remain limited to a 31-day window per call, which can be placed within retained history. Guarded SQL can query retained raw rows under its existing result, time and scan limits. Other page pickers and experiment result windows retain their existing limits.

 

Extended storage costs one weighted event per stored event older than 90 days each month, including synthetic traffic. This uses the studio's shared included event allowance first, then prepaid balance. At the current rate, one million older events use one million weighted events, at most $0.50 per month after the allowance. Enabling extended storage requires the owner's recurring-charge confirmation. The displayed estimate uses the current older-event count; future volume can change.

 

A longer window requires a positive prepaid balance. Before extending it, Ravensight settles pending monthly storage snapshots, including the current month's snapshot, using the included allowance first. If funds cannot cover the work, the longer window is not applied. Retrying resumes the same payment records without charging completed work twice.

 

For an existing extended window, refused payment starts a 14-day grace period. Add balance or resolve the usage limit before the deadline. If payment still cannot finish, retention returns to 90 days and older raw events expire. Switching tiers, including a return to 90 days, does not erase an unpaid snapshot or reset its grace. Free 90-day retention remains available; completed storage charges remain.

 

Dashboard account authentication is required for `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/games/{gameId}/retention`. Both are owner-only. A PUT accepts `{"retentionDays":180,"recurringConsent":true}`; 90 days does not require recurring consent. Shared-game viewers and studio admins cannot authorize these charges.

documents.section_title: What data Ravensight holds
documents.title: What data Ravensight holds
documents.content:
Programmatic access

 

## What data Ravensight holds

 

Every kind of data Ravensight stores for a studio, how long it is kept, and the [MCP tools](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/mcp/) that read or write it. Each read is checked against your studio, your role and your token on every call, so a tool only ever returns your own studio's records.

 

Every tool below costs one programmatic call, 100,000 weighted events on the shared event meter, and needs a studio that has funded a prepaid balance. A tool marked (write) also needs a token an owner allowed to write. This list is generated from the code that stores and serves the data. Any agent can read it, free, as the MCP resource `ravensight://data-products`, or as [JSON](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/data-products.json).

documents.section_title: What data Ravensight holds
documents.title: Player data
documents.content:
### Player data

 

| Data | What it holds, and its tools | Kept |

Event retention rules: kept until deleted. Event purges: kept 400 days. Event history imports: each record carries its own expiry. |

documents.section_title: Studio data
documents.title: Studio data
documents.content:
Your studio

 

## Studio data

 

Everything Ravensight holds for your studio, and how fresh it is. Open **Studio > Studio data** in the dashboard, or ask from your own agent with `describe_studio_data` over [MCP](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/mcp/).

documents.section_title: Studio data
documents.title: What it shows
documents.content:
### What it shows

 

One row for each kind of data in [what data Ravensight holds](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/data-products/), grouped the same way: player data, commercial, development, studio memory and operations. Each row gives how many records of that kind your studio has, when something was last added, how long it is kept, and a link to the page that holds it. Events are one total across the games in view over the last 30 days; the per game counts are in the `games` list that `describe_studio_data` returns. A row with nothing in it reads Nothing yet.

 

It reads counts and dates only, never the records themselves: no event properties, sale amounts, post text or document bodies. It reads your own studio only, through the same membership checks as every other studio read. The retention text comes from the same generated list as the table above, so the two cannot disagree.

documents.section_title: Studio data
documents.title: All games or one game
documents.content:
### All games or one game

 

With one game picked in the switcher, this page counts that title's games. Under All games it counts the whole studio, with a filter to narrow it to one title. Some counts are only made for the whole studio rather than for one title: sales, Pulse, brainstorms, marketing touchpoints and similar records. A one-game view leaves those uncounted instead of guessing which share is the game's, so choose All games in the switcher to see them. Every member sees every project in the studio. Only an MCP token can be limited to some projects, and such a token is refused by `describe_studio_data`, because it reads the whole studio.

 

A count that could not be read, for example because a store was briefly unavailable, is shown as not counted, never as zero. Results are cached for up to five minutes, so a record you just added may take that long to appear.

documents.section_title: Studio data
documents.title: Needs attention
documents.content:
### Needs attention

 

Above the rows, Studio data lists what needs your attention, each with a link to the place that fixes it. Nothing here charges you or starts a payment.

 

- **A connection that needs attention:** repeated failed syncs or a key to re-enter. One failed sync is retried and does not show here, and this hint appears only in the whole studio view. Open [Connections](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/connections/) in Settings to see why and, for a refused key, paste a new one.
 
- **Events about to start aging out.** A game whose oldest events reach its retention limit (90, 180 or 400 days) within the next 30 days. The hint shows only in that window: once removal has started it is the normal state for a game older than its retention, so there is no hint. Lifetime totals survive; [extended retention](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/extended-retention/) keeps the events themselves.
 
- **An unfunded account.** MCP reads need a studio that has funded a prepaid balance at least once, so your own agents are refused until it has. See [usage, billing and limits](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/limits/).

documents.section_title: Studio data
documents.title: What it costs
documents.content:
### What it costs

 

The dashboard page is included, with no charge. Over MCP, `describe_studio_data` is one metered read: 100,000 weighted events on the shared event meter, drawn from the included monthly events first and then the prepaid balance, and it needs a studio that has funded a prepaid balance. It reads the whole studio, so a token limited to some projects is refused, and a refused call is not charged. Huginn, the AI analyst, can use it inside the one AI unit a question already costs.

documents.section_title: Import event history
documents.title: Import event history
documents.content:
## Import event history

 

Moving to Ravensight from another analytics tool? Export its events as a CSV file and import them into your game. Imported events land in the game's own events as real players' events, so every page, [SQL](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/warehouse-sql/) and the [MCP tools](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/mcp/) read them beside the events your game sends.

documents.section_title: Import event history
documents.title: Which days can take events
documents.content:
### Which days can take events

 

Raw events are kept for 90 days, and an imported day has its daily and monthly totals, new players and retention rebuilt from raw events. So a day can take imported events only when that rebuild can never lower what is already stored for it:

 

- Days from 87 days back through yesterday. The last three days of the 90 day window are left alone, because a session there may have started on a day that is already gone, and today is still being counted.
 
- A day with no stored history, which is the usual case for events from before your game sent live ones, is always open.
 
- A day that already has stored history is closed when a rule to [keep an event shorter](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/event-catalogue/), or a purge, removed events from it, or when its raw events no longer add up to what was counted for it.

 

The check gives the first day this game can take, and refuses a row on a closed day as `day_not_rebuildable`.

documents.section_title: Import event history
documents.title: What a file needs
documents.content:
### What a file needs

 

A CSV export with a header row, up to 20 MB and 50,000 rows. Every row needs three columns; the rest are optional.

 

| Field | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `timestamp` | When the event happened: an ISO 8601 date and time (a time with no zone reads as UTC), or unix seconds or milliseconds. Required. |
| `event` | The event name, up to 200 characters. Required. |
| `player` | A player, user or device identifier. Required. It is never stored; see [Players and privacy](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/#history-import-privacy). |
| `properties` | The event's properties as one JSON object. |
| `session` | A session identifier. Without one, a player's events start a new session after 30 minutes without an event. |
| `level` | The level, stage or map the event happened in. |
| `platform` | The platform the game ran on, up to 128 characters. |
| `game_version` | The game or app version, up to 128 characters. |

 

Any other column can be kept as a property named by its header, stored as text, or ignored. A column whose header names personal data (such as email, phone, IP address, address, first, last or full name, or username) cannot be kept, and neither can a header that starts with `rs_`.

documents.section_title: Import event history
documents.title: Importing from the dashboard
documents.content:
### Importing from the dashboard

 

1. Open **Events** for the game and press **Import history**. Owners and admins see it; it is not offered on a game another studio shared with you.
 
1. Choose the file and press **Read the file**. Ravensight proposes a column for each field it recognises. A column marked **Suggested** is a guess for you to confirm; a column nobody recognised starts on **Ignore this column**. Only the column headers and the shape of their values are used for suggestions, never the values themselves.
 
1. Press **Check the file**. Ravensight reads every row under your mapping and shows the rows read, the new events to import, the rows already imported, the refused rows by reason with their line numbers, the date range, the number of players and the price. It also warns when days in the file already have live events from your game: if the same play was sent live too, it would count twice. Nothing is written or charged by a check. Change the mapping and check again to see what the new mapping does.
 
1. Press **Import**. Imported events show an **Imported** tag on the Events page. Totals, new players, monthly history and retention for the imported days are rebuilt right after, usually within minutes.

 

One history import runs at a time per studio. A second one started meanwhile is refused with `history_import_running` and changes nothing; start it again once the first has finished. A game cannot be deleted while an import into it is running.

documents.section_title: Import event history
documents.title: What happens to each row
documents.content:
### What happens to each row

 

Every row is held to the same rules as an event your game sends: typed events (purchases, resources, progression, errors, health, ads, attribution) are checked and flagged the same way, the level is read from `level`, `location` or `track`, and an event's data may be up to 8 KB. Country and device fields are never filled in for an imported event. A row that cannot be imported is refused with its line and one of these reasons, and the rest of the file is still imported. Two identical lines in a file are two events, as the export lists them. A file with two columns of the same name is refused as a whole (`duplicate_header`): rename one and read it again.

 

| Reason | When |
| --- | --- |
| `no_timestamp` | The timestamp cell is empty. |
| `bad_timestamp` | The timestamp is not ISO 8601, unix seconds or unix milliseconds, or names a date that does not exist. |
| `too_old` | The event is older than 90 days. |
| `day_not_rebuildable` | The event is on a day that cannot take imported events; see [Which days can take events](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/#history-import-window). |
| `in_future` | The event is later than now. |
| `bad_name` | The event name is empty, longer than 200 characters, or has control characters. |
| `no_player` | The player cell is empty. |
| `bad_player` | The player or session cell is longer than 256 characters. |
| `bad_properties` | The properties cell is not a JSON object. |
| `reserved_key` | The properties set `rs_import`, `rs_event_id` or `rs_link`, which Ravensight writes itself. |
| `bad_value` | The level, platform or game version is longer than 128 characters or has control characters. |
| `too_large` | The event's data is more than 8 KB. |
| `error_capture_off` | An automatic error, while error capture is off for the game. |
| `too_many_cells` | The row has more than 200 cells. |
| `already_imported` | The same line of the file was imported before under a different mapping. |
| `storage_refused` | Event storage refused the row's data. It is not charged. |
| `changes_closed_day` | Importing the row would change a day that cannot take imported events: it continues a session already imported onto such a day, or it comes before its player's first day and that day is such a day. |
| `player_erased` | The player was erased; their rows are never imported again. |
| `row_limit` | Past the 50,000th row. |

documents.section_title: Import event history
documents.title: Players and privacy
documents.content:
### Players and privacy

 

The player identifier in the file is never stored. Each one becomes a private player id for this game, made with a one-way key that belongs to the game, so an email address in an export never appears in your events, and the same identifier in two games is two unrelated players. Session identifiers are treated the same way. Imported players are counted as their own players: they do not merge with devices your game's SDK reports.

 

Sessions carry across files. With no session column, a player's events that come within 30 minutes of an event already imported for them continue that session, so a session that crosses midnight, exported as two daily files, still counts once. A session identifier that comes back after a long gap starts a new session rather than counting the old one twice.

 

To erase an imported player, send the identifier as it appeared in the export: `POST /api/v1/games/{gameId}/devices/erase-imported` with `{"identifier": "..."}`. Ravensight works out the private id with the game's key and erases that player's events the same way it erases any player. Only the owner can erase, the identifier is not kept or logged, and the audit log records the erasure without it. An erased player stays erased: importing the same file again refuses their rows as `player_erased`. The same holds when you erase the private id itself with `DELETE /api/v1/games/{gameId}/devices/{deviceId}`, and you can erase a player before your first import, so the file you import afterwards leaves them out. While an import into the game is running, an erasure answers `409 history_import_running`: the player is already kept out of every later import, and you erase again once the running one finishes, within the hour.

 

Each imported event carries `rs_import`, the id of the import it came in by, so a filter, a SQL query or an export can tell imported events from live ones. A live event cannot set it.

documents.section_title: Import event history
documents.title: Importing again
documents.content:
### Importing again

 

Importing the same file again imports and charges nothing more: every event has a stable id made from its content, and every line of the file is remembered, so an event already imported is skipped, and the same lines under a different mapping are refused as `already_imported` rather than imported twice. An export that overlaps an earlier one imports only the events that are new. If an import stops part way (the balance ran out, or events could not be stored), import the same file again to finish it.

 

Now and then event storage does not confirm a batch it was sent. Those rows are reported as `uncertain`: the events they need stay held on your meter, not refunded and not charged twice, until Ravensight counts what event storage holds, keeps exactly that and releases the rest. The next import of the same file counts first and sends only the rows storage does not hold, so each event is stored and charged once. Left alone, an unconfirmed batch is settled by Ravensight within about two hours. In the rare case that event storage still holds only part of a batch a week later, the rows it holds are kept and charged, the rest are released so the same file imports them again, and the audit log records it as **Event history batch settled**.

documents.section_title: Import event history
documents.title: Price
documents.content:
### Price

 

Each imported event counts as one event on your shared event meter, the same as a live event: this month's included events first, then your prepaid balance in event blocks at the ordinary rate. There is no separate price for imports. The check shows the events an import would use and, to the owner, what it would draw from the balance; an admin is told it comes from the studio's prepaid balance, which only the owner can see. Each batch is held on the meter before it is written, so an empty balance stops the import before anything is stored; afterwards what event storage holds is kept and the rest of the hold released. Import writes events until the balance runs out, keeps and charges what was written, then stops; nothing past that point is written or charged. Add funds in Billing, then import the same file again to finish. Rows that are refused or already imported are free.

 

Imported events are left out of the lateness figures in data quality, and days with imported events are left out of market benchmarks, so neither reads old events as late or as live play.

documents.section_title: Import event history
documents.title: From an agent or the API
documents.content:
### From an agent or the API

 

With a dashboard session, `POST /api/v1/games/{gameId}/history-import/preview` takes `{"csv": "...", "mapping": {...}}` (the mapping is optional) or the CSV itself as `text/csv`, and answers the mapping, the summary and the price. `POST /api/v1/games/{gameId}/history-import` takes `{"csv": "...", "mapping": {...}}` and answers the import id and its counts. A mapping is `{ "header": "field" }` with the fields above, `carry` to keep a column as a property, or `ignore`. Both need an owner or admin; another studio's game answers 404, an empty balance answers `429 quota_exceeded` with `reason: "needs_funds"`, a game with tracking off answers `403 tracking_disabled`, and a second import while one runs answers `409 history_import_running`. A file that arrives slower than 100 KB a second (measured once its first 10 seconds have passed) or takes longer than 10 minutes in all answers `408 history_import_timeout`, a JSON body that is not one CSV string and one mapping object answers `400 invalid_body`, a compressed body (any `Content-Encoding`) answers `415 unsupported_encoding` (send the file uncompressed), a file whose players already have more than 200,000 imported events around its times answers `400 too_many_stored_neighbours` (import a narrower time range), and while other files are being read, or another of your studio's, the answer is `503 history_import_busy` with `Retry-After`. The import answers `imported`, `alreadyImported`, `uncertain`, `notImported` and `stopped` (why it stopped part way, or null).

 

Agents use `preview_event_history_import` and `import_event_history` over [MCP](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/mcp/), up to 1 MB of CSV per call. The import tool needs a token with writes allowed.

documents.section_title: Share analytics with another studio
documents.title: Share analytics with another studio
documents.content:
## Share analytics with another studio

 

In Settings, Team, the receiving studio owner creates an invitation code. Give it privately to the source studio owner, who opens Settings, Team or `/share/accept`, reviews the destination and explicitly selects games. The code expires after seven days and works once.

 

Recipients can read game analytics and digests, including cross-game comparisons and the breakdowns by country and device. They cannot change games, read ingest keys or configuration, ask the analyst, read feedback, or manage exports. Either studio owner can revoke access immediately. Sharing never transfers ownership.

 

API and MCP reads use the receiving token's studio allowance and balance. Project-restricted tokens cannot read shared games. Use a studio-scoped token with only the tools you need. Shared games are marked read only in the game list.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.content:
28. Usage, billing and limits

 

## What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe

 

Every feature is available on every account. Pricing is usage-based: a free monthly allowance, then metered rates for anything past it, drawn from a prepaid balance. Top-ups start at $5 and balances do not expire. Paid work stops when funds are unavailable unless optional auto-recharge adds funds.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Rates
documents.content:
### Rates

 

1,000,000 included events / month free 5 shared AI units / month included 90 day raw event retention

 

There are two units of account, events and AI units. Events are counted on one event meter: a player event or text report is 1 event, a screenshot report adds 20,000 and an MCP call is 100,000, and what Pulse and connections store is weighted by row, as below. One studio shares the monthly allowance across every project and every environment in it. Browsing saved dashboard data uses neither.

 

| What | Price | Included allowance? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Events on the meter past the allowance | $0.05 per started block of 100,000 | 1,000,000 a month |
| An AI unit past the allowance | $0.20 | 5 a month |
| Analyst question, Design chat turn, risk check, investigation analysis, digest, brainstorm question, strategy matrix suggestion, market research run, market research quick look, market draft | 1 AI unit each | Yes |
| Feedback enrichment | 1 AI unit per batch of up to 25 items | Yes |
| Pattern synthesis, the deep tier | 5 AI units ($1.00) | No, prepaid balance only |
| Deep market research | 25 AI units ($5.00) | No, prepaid balance only |
| Player Report | 1 event for the text, plus 20,000 events for a screenshot | Yes, as events |
| Pulse: each post, snapshot, comment and reaction stored | Post 1,000 events; snapshot 100; comment, reply or quote 300; reaction or repost 20; each read of a connected source 50. A row already stored costs nothing | Yes, as events |
| Pulse: Huginn's summary of a post's comments, or of a date range | 1 AI unit; asking again with no new comments is free | Yes |
| Pulse: reading a watched link | 1,000 events plus 1 event per byte read, at most 2 MB a read (about 2.1 million events) | Yes, as events |
| Connection sync | 500 events plus 1 event per byte read; each new sales row or snapshot 100, each new post 1,000 | Yes, as events |
| MCP call, read or write | 100,000 events ($0.05 past the allowance) | Yes, as events; needs an account that has funded a balance at least once |
| Exported event (bucket export) | 5 events per event exported (100,000 exported events are $0.25 past the allowance) | Yes, as events |
| Source scan, first scan | $5 under 250 KB, $10 under 1 MB, $25 under 4 MB, $50 under 16 MB | No, prepaid balance only |
| Source scan, rescan | $2 while the changed source is under 250 KB, otherwise its size tier; free when nothing changed | No, prepaid balance only |
| Playtest | $6.40 a persona run, $8.20 a long persona run, $8.40 a game profile, $18.60 a fix attempt. A persona run that ends short of 15 actions through no fault of the game, or that did not earn its price but used AI time, is billed at what it cost us | No, prepaid balance only |
| Cloud playtest, each persona | $3.60 Jam (5 minutes), $4.80 Small (8 minutes), $8.00 Medium (15 minutes), $15.80 Large (30 minutes, including a $1.00 non-refundable setup fee); a longer play length is priced by the quote, for example $28.80 for 60 minutes on Medium. A build too large for its tier keeps the time and model spend used plus a $2.00 fee | No, prepaid balance only. [Cloud playtests](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/playtest/#playtest-cloud) |
| Hosted Linux simulation | $6.09 a run, quoted as one total; the first run credits its $0.49 build deposit once | No, prepaid only; $10 initial verified funding, then enough available funds to cover each request. [Funding and refunds](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/playtest/#hosted-simulation) |

 

Each MCP call, read or write, is metered as 100,000 weighted events on the account-wide event meter, the same meter every game's player events draw from. At 100,000 events a call, the included 1,000,000 events cover about ten MCP calls in a month when nothing else is sent, and once MCP calls have used the allowance, every game's player events are billed from the first one. The usage page in **Settings > Billing** shows MCP calls as their own bar and line, and the sidebar meter gives them their own row, with the weighted events they were metered as and what that comes to at the event rate, beside the player events and text reports your games actually sent.

 

An agent can read the same thing without the dashboard: every metered MCP answer carries `_meta.remaining`, and `get_usage_rate` returns `allowance` and `balanceCents` (see [MCP](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/mcp/)). In a rate, `includedAllowance` refers to AI units only: MCP calls draw the included monthly events first, then the prepaid balance.

 

Source scans are quoted before they run. Playtest units are charged when a job registers and refunded for any unit that did not produce a usable result, including a persona run that ended early with no findings, and a fix attempt is refunded in full when it changed nothing, the finding was design intent, or the game did not boot for its verify run (up to twice in any 30 days per account, with CLI 0.6.0 or later). Once the model has been used, an account gets 5 refunds of a fix attempt, 5 of a game profile and 20 of a persona run in any 30 days. Past that the unit is kept and the job says so; work that used no model time always comes back. Failed, undelivered AI work is refunded.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Rate limits
documents.content:
### Rate limits

 

Per game, per 60 second window: 60 session creations and 600 tracked events. A batch call costs one unit per event, capped at the 50-event batch ceiling, so a full batch never charges more than a valid batch could. Both the versioned and legacy ingestion paths share the same budget for a given game. A [public key](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/public-builds/) adds its own limits per key, per session and per device id below these. `GET /api/v1/settings` allows 30 reads a minute per key and connecting address.

 

Every rate limit is counted on the API server that answers the request, not in a shared store. Ravensight runs one API server today, so these figures are the limits your game sees. If more servers are added, a limit applies on each server separately until this page says otherwise.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Payload ceilings
documents.content:
### Payload ceilings

 

Request bodies are capped at 100KB, except `/track` and `/track/batch`, which take 512KB so a full batch of error events with their stacks fits. Those two accept a body sent with `Content-Encoding: gzip` or `deflate`; the 512KB is counted after it is decoded, and any other encoding answers `415 unsupported_encoding`. Within them, an event name is capped at 200 characters and one event's data at 8KB serialized (a typed `error` event's `rs_message`, `rs_stack` and `rs_trail` count one byte a character there, so a stack of up to 2,000 characters always fits): events are gameplay facts, not documents. A batch containing one oversized event, or a batch past the request cap, answers 400, and every SDK halves the batch until it fits, isolating and dropping an offending event automatically, so a single bloated event never costs the rest of its batch. Feedback messages are capped at 2,000 characters.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Data retention
documents.content:
### Data retention

 

Raw events are kept for 90 days by default; an owner can choose 180 or 400 days with [extended retention](https://www.ravensight.io/docs/extended-retention/). Before events age out, Ravensight extracts daily and monthly aggregates (active players, new players, sessions, events, top events, level funnels, cohort retention) and keeps those forever, along with lifetime totals per game. The 1y and All views in the dashboard, and the analyst's long-range answers, are served from these aggregates, even with extended raw storage. Guarded SQL via run_sql and the warehouse endpoint can read raw rows still retained for the game, subject to their execution limits. History collection can be switched off per environment in **Settings > Projects**; production, early access and demo environments keep it on by default, because the public plays them; alpha, beta, staging, development and custom environments start with it off.

 

One consequence worth knowing: the aggregates are computed from real player sessions only, and carry no column saying which rows an AI persona produced. So the long-range history endpoints take no persona scope at all, because there is nothing there to include. Your 1y and All numbers are real players, always. The **Real players** select applies to raw-event views; it does not add synthetic traffic to historical rollups.

 

Raw event export

 

```
GET /api/v1/games/<gameId>/analytics/events/export?after=0&skip=0&limit=10000
Cookie: gt_session (dashboard sign-in)

{ "events": [ { "deviceId", "sessionId", "event", "ts", "level",
               "platform", "gameVersion", "data",
               "schema", "gameId", "tsIso", "synthetic", "props",
               "rs" }, ... ],
  "nextAfter": 1755648000123, "nextSkip": 3 }
```

 

Oldest first, up to 10,000 events per page; keep requesting with `after = nextAfter` and `skip = nextSkip` until `nextAfter` is null. Events can share a timestamp, and `skip` is how many events at that timestamp you already have, so no page boundary drops or repeats one. Export anything you want to keep beyond the game's selected raw-event retention window.

 

The first eight keys are unchanged. Each event also carries `schema` (the row format version, currently 1), `gameId`, `tsIso` (the timestamp as UTC ISO text), `synthetic` (true for a playtest session, which the export leaves out unless you ask), `props` (the event's top-level properties as text) and `rs`. The `rs` object is the typed event contract read back: `kind` is the `rs_kind` you sent (or null), and a purchase, resource, progression, error or health event adds a `purchase`, `resource`, `progression`, `error` or `health` object with its fields. A purchase `amount` is a string of whole minor units, and resource amounts, scores and health metrics are decimal text, exactly as stored. An event that broke the contract carries `rs.invalid` with the reason and no field object. Events also carry `country`, `deviceModel`, `osVersion` and `gpu` from the session, and `campaign`, `adset` and `creative` from the device's acquisition record; each is null when unknown. Keys are only ever added to this shape, so read the ones you know and ignore the rest.

documents.section_title: What everything costs, and the limits that keep it safe
documents.title: Safety ceiling
documents.content:
### Safety ceiling

 

There is a safety ceiling of 500,000,000 events a month per account, which applies even with a balance loaded. It exists so a runaway loop or a broken build cannot turn a prepaid balance into hundreds of millions of events you never meant to send, and it is checked before anything is charged, so a refused batch costs nothing. Past it you get the same `429 quota_exceeded`, with a message saying it is the ceiling rather than the allowance. If that volume is genuinely yours, ask and we will raise it.

 

AI actions use Ravensight-managed providers and the shared prepaid balance. Customers do not supply provider API keys.
